title: Tour Route Intent
user: Self-supported touring cyclists who know the roads or paths they want but need a route file that preserves those deliberate choices across navigation apps.

evidence.quote_or_summary: A route planner keeps reconnecting waypoints onto an unwanted path; the requester wants it to preserve a known walking route between deliberate points.
A beginner asks what long-term bicycle tourists wish they knew about route planning, breakdowns, packing, budgets, and logistics.

recurrence: Route planning is a named concern for both a navigation user and prospective long-distance tourists; a wrong reroute can put a loaded rider onto unsuitable roads.
current_workaround: Add many waypoints, hand-draw a GPX in a desktop planner, and hope the phone app does not silently re-route during navigation.
incumbents_and_gap: Komoot, RideWithGPS, and Organic Maps plan routes well; they do not universally preserve the rider's rationale for an intentional detour, surface choice, or resupply constraint in a portable route artifact.
smallest_useful_product: Static web GPX planner that lets a user lock segments/waypoints and attach terse intent notes (surface, water, ferry, avoid-at-night), then validates whether an exported route still passes them. Non-goals: turn-by-turn navigation, live traffic, or map-data scraping.
success_measure: In a field test, 90% of exported routes retain every locked segment when imported into two target navigation apps.
monetization: one-time — route preparation is an occasional planning task and the export must remain usable without a hosted account.
constraints: Use openly licensed map tiles/data only; make routing-engine limitations explicit; no safety guarantee; location notes remain in the exported local file unless shared.
why_distinct: It protects deliberate route intent across tools rather than replacing a full navigation product.
